text: So when we could bear it no longer, we were willing to be left behind alone in Athens,

versions.text: So when we could bear it no longer, we decided to be left behind at Athens alone,
versions.explanation: "at Athens" is archaic for oral reading; "in Athens" flows more naturally. Also εὐδοκήσαμεν carries the sense of "were willing/thought it best" rather than a bare decision.

text: and we sent Timothy, our brother and God's coworker in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and encourage you in your faith,
so that no one would be shaken by these troubles. For you yourselves know that this is what we are appointed to.

versions.text: so that no one would be shaken by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that this is what we are destined for.
versions.explanation: "destined for" may suggest fatalism; κείμεθα means "we are appointed/set for this." Also "troubles" reads more naturally aloud than repeating "afflictions" alongside verse 4 and 7.

text: In fact, when we were with you, we told you in advance that we would be afflicted—and so it happened, as you know.
That is why, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to find out about your faith, afraid that the tempter had tempted you and that our labor might prove to be in vain.

versions.text: That is why, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, fearing that the tempter had tempted you and that our labor had come to nothing.
versions.explanation: The second clause is a subjunctive (γένηται), expressing a feared possibility, not a completed fact; "might prove to be in vain" better renders it.

text: But now Timothy has come to us from you, bringing good news of your faith and love, and reporting that you always remember us kindly and long to see us, just as we long to see you.
For this reason, brothers, in all our distress and affliction we have been comforted about you through your faith,
because now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
How can we thank God enough for you, for all the joy we have because of you in the presence of our God,

versions.text: What thanks can we render to God for you, for all the joy we feel because of you before our God,
versions.explanation: "render" is stiff for oral reading, and "the joy we feel" is weaker than the Greek's "joy we rejoice with"; "before our God" is clearer as "in the presence of our God."

text: as night and day we pray most earnestly that we may see you face to face and complete what is lacking in your faith?

versions.text: as night and day we pray most earnestly that we may see you face to face and supply what is lacking in your faith?
versions.explanation: καταρτίσαι means to mend, complete, or put right rather than simply "supply"; "complete" better conveys the sense of bringing the faith to maturity.

text: Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, clear the way for us to come to you.
And may the Lord make your love increase and overflow for one another and for everyone, just as ours does for you,
so that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.
